items.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025
items.q: the thing with Glenn Drewes and me... We were all close.

ctx.x: Right. You didn’t understand the language.

They didn’t work on it first of all, hard enough, because they may be first trumpet in some orchestra and somebody asked them to make a recording of it and they could play it, physically they were fine trumpet players. But the most important thing, and that’s another reason why I used the books that I could teach them this, to the band directors and to the people who were going to be professional trumpet players. See because it’s the same. You’re teaching music. You know? They have to be musically strong and then…

average as it always did. And then he’d look at us and never stop the band. And I’d say, “Glen, I think we did something wrong.” Because that’s all he would do. He’d never call us out in band. But you know people couldn’t play the same part — he never said anything to them because he knew why they were in band. So it became a really inclusive band. We were all close. The ones that played well and the ones that didn’t. And then I’d go home I’d say, “Mom, he looked at me today.” She knew what that meant. You know…
